title: A polynomial-time construction of strong thin trees
main_claim: Deterministic polynomial-bit-time algorithm that, given a k-edge-connected multigraph (explicit or with binary multiplicities), outputs a spanning tree that is C/k-thin for an absolute constant C (algorithmic strong thin-tree conjecture).

issues.description: The move from the companion's cube/cut geometry to the metric-cone polytope Q is given as a proof sketch. It checks the geometric primitives (disjoint balls, exact radial motion, the edge-segment charging, conflict domains) but takes the scalar accounting and the case constructions from companion Propositions B.7–B.20 and Lemmas B.13–B.20 without repeating them. The final hierarchy bound therefore stands only if those companion arguments are correct and really use nothing beyond the primitives checked here. I did not re-verify them.
issues.evidence: Text such as 'We retain those constructions and their scalar accounting', 'The radial count in the cited proof gives m>=3(C_3-1)...', and 'The source's width calculation bounds the lost potential by half the inserted mass'. The geometric replacements I did check: disjoint balls via midpoint convexity, exact radial motion from the doubled profiles, and ||Y_u-Y_v||^2 <= d(u,v) giving disjointness from the companion's spectral lemma (which needs squared separation > 4r).

coverage:
I read the whole paper except the fractional-rounding corollary (not part of the main result). I checked each step of the following line by line.
- Iteration (Sec. iteration): the one-step sparsification lemma; the telescoping product with r_{i+1} <= r_i/2, giving bounded sum of r_i^{-1/16}; the initial floor(k/2) tree packing; the binary-multiplicity reduction (cut lower bound 2n^2 - n^2/4, the n^4 edge count, lifting back to original edges).
- Projected-trace packing argument: rank preservation gives rank Pi >= d-1, then Nash–Williams.
- Log-determinant frame lemma: AM-GM lower bound, Hessian = tree-indicator covariance, descent decrease constant, termination gradient bound, and ||z_e||^2 <= (1+4/r)/q.
- Signing lemma: block Cauchy–Schwarz giving <= 2I, exact rational padding (the tau cross-terms cancel), V D_0 V^T removal, final constant 2^20.
- Extraction: the ramp lower-bound algebra (rechecked the numerator identity); the uncrossing/tie-break argument showing the minimizer's support is a chain; the near-tight partitions having h-connected parts; the gain/loss computation in both cases.
- Ellipsoid step: auxiliary interior point margins, mixing with theta = P^-8, inradius P^-30, and the eta/gamma grid-rounding inequality Dγ/2 <= η/(2P).
- Prop tg-response: Y = L_H + D lies in K_H; Markov bound; dyadic-bin counting giving 4M_i, 8(...) and 16(...); exponent 21/40 > 1/3.
- Hierarchy-theorem parameter arithmetic: exponents -23/25 and 32/5, the assignment and rho conditions, c_* = 1/320000.
- Conic dual lemma: nuclear-norm bound and Cauchy–Schwarz.
- Signing appendix: potential bounds and the constant 40 > 2√386 · √1.001; the freeze-step inequality; Bansal–Garg dimension/trace count 23n/48. I verified the scalar inequalities of eq. sign-scalar numerically (400k random samples, no violations).
- Not re-verified: the companion's Appendix B constructions and the Ezeunala–Jiang 2026 analysis.
sibling_notes: No sibling entries existed for family 174 when I checked. This paper depends heavily on the companion 'The strong thin tree conjecture' (same release): its Appendix B bag/charging propositions, spectral packing Lemma B.3 (C_1 = 1024/eps^2, which matches), and Lemma 4.2 (dyadic assembly). Whoever audits the companion's hierarchy_bags*/hierarchy_assigned*/hierarchy_compact sections is effectively auditing the one unverified dependency here.
